prompt: Leave the voicemail Dad leaves after seeing a truck for sale that looks just like your old one.
response:
Hey bud, it’s Dad. Don’t worry, nobody’s hurt, nothing’s broken.

I was just driving past that lot on Route 9 and I swear I had to pull over. There’s a ’98 F-150 sitting right by the fence, and it’s your old blue one. Not *a* blue one. *Your* blue one. Same faded spot on the tailgate where you backed into the mailbox learning to park, same dent above the passenger wheel well from that camping trip. Even has that crooked chrome trim you never got around to fixing.

I know we sold it six years ago. I know the engine was knocking and the cab smelled like wet dog and motor oil by the end. But standing there looking at it… I could suddenly hear you laughing in the backseat when you were little, kicking the seat every time we hit a bump. Felt like I could still smell that coffee stain on the floor mat from your first solo drive to campus.

Anyway. I didn’t call the number on the window. I just stood there for a minute, then got back in my car. Didn’t need to own it again to remember. Just wanted to tell you I saw it, and that I’m proud of the man who learned to drive in that rattly old thing.

Call your mother when you get this. She’ll want to hear about it too. Love you, kiddo.
